subject: Escrow mechanics & billing proration — Exhibit C fee-collar question
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Rivera <sofia.rivera@novushealth.com>, procure@novushealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-22T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Escrow mechanics & billing proration — Exhibit C fee-collar question

Hi Sofia / procurement team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We reviewed your redline to Exhibit C and had a couple of operational clarifications we want to confirm before we push the counter-redline back to legal. Two specific items: 

1) Source of escrow funding: Exhibit C references an "escrow pool" to cover fee-collar shortfalls. Is Novus expecting that the escrow is funded up-front as a separate escrow deposit line item, or that Redwood withholds future invoices/credits against the first N invoices until the escrow target is reached? The operational handling changes tax and billing flows.

2) Proration and true-up timing: Your redline requires quarterly true-ups, but also says the escrow draw can be initiated at any time after a quarter where actual usage < floor. Do you expect partial prorated draws mid-quarter or only at quarterly true-up windows? If mid-quarter draws are permitted, we want to confirm whether that will generate interim invoices/credit memos or be netted against the next invoice.

I've attached a spreadsheet that lays out three operational flows (up-front deposit, invoice withholding, and cashless netting) and the downstream invoice events we think will occur. Can you confirm which you prefer so we can update Exhibit C wording to match the operational picture?

Attachments: [FeeCollar_Escrow_v2.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)]

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Mark Chen <mark.chen@novushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Rivera <sofia.rivera@novushealth.com>, procure@novushealth.com
Date: 2025-10-22T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escrow mechanics & billing proration — Exhibit C fee-collar question

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the spreadsheet. A few quick answers from legal/procurement perspective: 

- Novus prefers the escrow to be cash-backed up-front (one-time deposit tied to the order schedule) for the first 12 months to avoid complexity with revenue recognition across multiple vendors. We can consider invoice withholding only if Redwood can provide a monthly statement and an auditable ledger for the escrow.

- Regarding draws: our expectation is that escrow draws are only reconciled at quarterly true-ups. We do not want ad-hoc mid-quarter draws unless there is a material billing dispute. That said, the redline we provided allowed for interim draws in limited circumstances; we can remove that clause if Redwood wants to commit to the quarterly cadence.

I've attached the redline excerpt.

Mark Chen
Sr. Counsel, Novus Health
mark.chen@novushealth.com
[Attachment: Exhibit-C_redline.docx]

On Wed, Oct 22, 2025 at 09:02 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (see below)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-22T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escrow mechanics & billing proration — Exhibit C fee-collar question

Jordan / Karthik —

Thanks for flagging. Operational notes:

- Up-front deposit (Option A): straightforward from our side but requires finance to treat the deposit as deferred revenue until drawn. Acceptable for Enterprise deals but requires a payment term amendment on the order.

- Invoice withholding (Option B): We can implement a manual withholding (apply credits) until the escrow amount is reached. This is operationally heavier (credit memos, monthly reconciliations) but avoids Novus sending an up-front wire. We will need a definitive ledger export and a GL mapping to support audits.

- Cashless netting (Option C): Most frictionless for both parties: no upfront cash, Redwood withholds/credits monthly and any shortfalls are reconciled at quarterly true-up. This is how we typically handle smaller customers but Novus asked for cash-backed escrow for the first 12 months.

Recommendation: Offer Novus Option A but include a concession to accept Option B if Novus provides a signed SLA for monthly ledger export and commits to a 60-day window for disputed items. We can also propose an onboarding credit (one-time equivalent of up to $25k) to offset their preference for cash escrow.

I've drafted proposed redline language for Exhibit C in the attached spreadsheet and also added suggested language to the order schedule PDF. See attachments: [FeeCollar_Escrow_v2.xlsx, Novus-OrderSchedule-v1.pdf]

Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Rivera <sofia.rivera@novushealth.com>, Mark Chen <mark.chen@novushealth.com>, procure@novushealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-22T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escrow mechanics & billing proration — Exhibit C fee-collar question

Sofia / Mark —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. To keep the contract moving and minimize accounting lift on your side, Redwood can agree to Option A (cash-backed up-front) for the first 12 months as requested. In exchange, Redwood requests: 

- Novus to sign the payment term amendment reflecting the deposit schedule on the order (we show a one-time deposit equal to one quarter's forecasted floor).
- If Novus prefers not to wire, we can do invoice withholding (Option B) but require the monthly ledger export and a 60-day dispute window as Laura noted.
- As a commercial sweetener, we will apply a one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 to Novus's first invoice (credit applies after escrow deposit is posted).

If that works, we'll incorporate the Exhibit C language changes and send a clean counter-redline and DocuSign packet for signatures.

Thanks,
Jordan

[Attachment: FeeCollar_Escrow_v2.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-10-23T09:22:00-07:00

Jordan / team —

Legal is okay with the proposal but asks for very tight wording to avoid ambiguity around when escrow funds are considered "drawn" vs. "credited." Proposed short clause: 

"Escrow deposit shall be held as cash-backed collateral. Escrow draws may be executed only at the time of quarterly true-up and shall be evidenced by a signed adjustment summary. An interim administrative credit may be posted to Customer invoices pending reconciliation, but no final draw shall occur outside the quarterly true-up process unless mutually agreed in writing by both parties."

I also approved the one-time $25,000 onboarding credit for commercial sign-off; please document as a separate line on the first invoice with reference to Deal ID DEAL-9342.

I'll prepare a short counter-redline for Exhibit C and upload to the HubSpot deal record. Once Novus confirms, we can route the DocuSign (link below).
